confirmed_issues.issue: SG11 cos-operand regression guard is structurally gate-blind in CI. The ONLY discriminating instrument (run_sg11_warmup_gate, tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:882 — requires >=1 warm-up step so cos(grad,mu) != cos(grad,momentum), the only check that can tell the buggy operand from the canonical one) is reachable ONLY via the --sg11-warmup CLI flag (main():1476-1499). The sole @pytest-collected SG11 entry, test_l3tc_cell_gate (:1457, parametrized over _CELLS), runs run_cell_gate -> the COLD step-1 path, which the file's own docstring (:883-887) admits is BLIND (at step 1 exp_avg=0 => cos(grad,mu)==cos(grad,momentum)==gate(0.5), the exact coincidence that hid the original SG11 bug). The static guard scripts/check_math_single_source.py compounds this: _cosine_consumer_headers() (:223-226) returns ONLY opt_stages_precompute.cuh and only scans for a re-inlined den_m/den_g += x*x loop (_COSINE_REINLINE_PATTERNS) — it does NOT inspect the 3 megakernel call-site operand pointers (fused_{decoder,vit,mamba}_megakernel.cuh), so a regression passing st.exp_avg_sq or st.mu instead of st.exp_avg into the canonical sg11_sweep_a_step would pass BOTH the static guard AND the entire pytest suite undetected. CONFIRMED at HEAD: git log 51098e0..HEAD -- tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py is EMPTY, so the commit message's own load-bearing FOLLOW-UP ('wire run_sg11_warmup_gate into a pytest-collected hw test ... next commit') is NOT done. Per the task's SG11-incident framing ('it passed the gate' is not sufficient), this is the residual gate-blind surface in production: the CI gate set CANNOT catch a recurrence of this exact bug class, and the discriminating gate exists in-tree but is not wired in. NOTE: this is a regression-GUARD gap, not a wrong kernel — the currently shipped kernel is correct.
confirmed_issues.action: Close the deferred FOLLOW-UP: (1) wrap run_sg11_warmup_gate in a @pytest.mark.hw test parametrized over the 3 SG11 cells, asserting ok AND gate_div>1e-4 AND momentum_norm>>0 (so it fails on the mu / exp_avg_sq / post-update-momentum operands); (2) extend scripts/check_math_single_source.py to assert each of the 3 megakernel SG11 call sites passes st.exp_avg (not st.exp_avg_sq / st.mu) as the momentum operand to sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor. issues.issue: The parity gate validates ONLY the shipped PIPE=1/STAGES=4 point against the fp64/eager oracle. There is NO direct PIPE=1-vs-PIPE=0 A/B numeric diff and NO PIPE/STAGES sweep in CI (the JIT TC TU compiles the baked defaults with no -D override; PIPE=0 is the designated byte-identical revert target but is never numerically re-confirmed equal to PIPE=1, and PIPE=2 is compiled-out by default). So the headline 'bit-identical-by-construction to PIPE=0' claim rests on the source argument, not on an executed A/B equality check. I re-derived that argument and it holds (see notes), so this is NOT a present wrong-kernel — but it is the SG11-class residual surface: a future edit to the ring that introduced a small fp32-reorder could pass the rel-1e-4 fp64 gate while silently NOT being bit-identical, because the gate floor (1e-4) is looser than 'bit-identical' and there is no construction-checking A/B/PTX guard on this branch.

Today the construction is genuinely order-preserving so the gate is honest, but nothing in CI enforces that it stays so (no ascending-k/byte-identity assertion, no PIPE sweep).

reports.notes:
VERDICT: the decoder bake (5c73b5d) is SOUND. No gate-blind correctness defect found. Re-verified the actual code at HEAD (git show 5c73b5d + the live .cuh files), not just the commit message.

(a) DYNAMIC-SMEM + 1-CTA/SM for ALL 11 optimizers — CONFIRMED. SG_DEC_TC_DYNAMIC_SMEM = (PIPE && STAGES>2) = (1 && 4>2) = 1 (fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:464), so the shipped config genuinely takes the dynamic path. The kernel (fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt>, :672) and launcher (launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt>, :1512) are BOTH templated on Opt; mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu:199-369 routes every one of the 11 OptIds (incl. Muon/LookSAM/SuperGrok11/15/2) through that single launcher. The cudaFuncSetAttribute opt-in (:1533, sized to sizeof(DecTcSmem)) AND the cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor cert (:1541) are per-<Opt>, and cudaOccupancy automatically folds in each instantiation's STATIC smem (incl. the SG11/SG15-only sg_sW1/sb1/sW2 static buffers at :1338-1340) + register pressure. A heavy cell that cannot place 1 CTA/SM returns cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources (LOUD refuse, :1545) — never a silent wrong answer. No second extern __shared__ exists, so the dynamic pool (sg_dectc_pool, :688) cannot alias the static buffers (dynamic smem is allocated past static on sm_90).

(b) BIT-IDENTICAL-BY-CONSTRUCTION — CONFIRMED (and the gate pass is NOT a coincidence). The deeper-ring branch (RS=3..4, :1017-1062) and the RS<=2 branch (:988-1016) BOTH call the identical issue_k(g_atoms,k,RS) (:750) in ascending k, k=0 ScaleD=0 overwrite / k>0 ScaleD=1 accumulate into the SAME acc[ai] fragments. RS only changes sl=k%RS (which slot the SAME tile-k operand bytes were staged into); the wgmma ISSUE sequence and fp32 accumulation order are unchanged. Only the cp.async prefetch DISTANCE (WHEN a tile lands) differs — a load reorder, not a math reorder. WAR-safety holds: refill of iter k writes slot (k-1)%RS, which was last read by wgmma(k-1) and drained by that iter's wgmma_wait_group<0> (:1055) before this iter's top barrier; the in-flight count is exactly RS-1 in steady (wait_group<RS-2>) and drains fully in the tail (wait_group<0>). Independently corroborated by the roadmap rank-4 refutation, which proves the per-K wait_group<0> is the load-bearing WAR fence (relaxing it to <1> would race). No reduction-order subtlety in the present code.

(c) NO INTERACTION with the SG11 fix or dW. The SG11 fix (51098e0) touches ONLY the P3 optimizer tail cosine-gate operand (st.mu -> st.exp_avg in sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor); the deeper ring is the P1 fwd / P2.4 dX GEMM — orthogonal phases. Because the ring never touches the optimizer tail, the SG11 cells' PIPE=1-vs-PIPE=0 parity is identical regardless of the (now-fixed) cos-operand, so the deeper-ring gate was unaffected by the SG11 bug even though it was committed first. dW uses S=kDecTcStages=2 (NOT RS) for its slot modulus (stage_k :731, issue_k(...,S) :1074) and lives in a strict subset of the kDecRingStagesMax=max(4,2)=4 smem arena (:268); it runs as a separate engine call from fwd/dX, so no live-slot aliasing.

(d) PERF CLAIM consistent: 920.6->618.5ms = 1.487x ~= +1.49x; cumulative 1889->618 ~= 3.05x; PIPE=2 documented loss 857 vs 618. sizeof(DecTcSmem) is d-independent (kDecTcSmemB1 = TILE_N*16, TILE_N pinned 128), default-tile S=4 = 33.64KB < 48KB but still routed to dynamic by the STAGES>2 gate (harmless, comment :456-459), so the gate's smem certification transfers to production d=2048.

issues.issue: VERIFIED CORRECT (not a defect). The kernel fix matches the canonical algorithm. Canonical Python (supergrok11.py:4-6,91-92) and header (supergrok11.h:22-29,64,88-105) both define gate = sigmoid(gate_temp * cos_sim(grad, MOMENTUM)); the fix routes all 3 staged call sites through the single-source algo::sg11_sweep_a_step with st.exp_avg as the 2nd cosine operand, replacing the buggy cos(grad,mu). The fix DIRECTION is right (defended against the inverse possibility by reading the canonical source). Concern (a): exp_avg IS the start-of-step momentum at precompute time for ALL 3 models -- each tensor task is owned by exactly one CTA via work-steal next_block(), precompute (reads exp_avg) runs before the apply sg11_sweep_b_step writes it, and for SG11 no earlier phase writes exp_avg (only the Muon path writes muon_buf=st.exp_avg+off, a different OptId). Concern (b): the removed __syncthreads is safe -- the new loop reads momentum[gi] (an input) at each thread's own stride; mu_blob is no longer read back inside the loop; the caller's post-precompute __syncthreads is retained. Concern (d): SG15 is correctly untouched -- it has NO cosine gate (host scalar sigmoid(accuracy), supergrok15.h:11,85,102), so the operand class does not apply; SG2 uses separate sg2_meta_stages.

issues.gate_blind_why: The committed regression guard against the SG11 cos-operand bug class is the warm-up gate, but it is CLI-only and never collected by pytest/CI. The only auto-collected test is the cold step-1 gate, which is mathematically incapable of distinguishing the buggy operand (step-1 coincidence: m=0 => both formulations give gate=0.5). The static check_math_single_source.py guard only scans opt_stages_precompute.cuh for a re-inlined den_m+=x*x loop and the supergrok11.h #include; it does NOT inspect the 3 megakernel call-site arguments, so a regression that calls sg11_sweep_a_step with the wrong pointer (st.exp_avg_sq or st.mu instead of st.exp_avg) would pass the static guard AND the pytest gate. So 'it passed the gate' remains insufficient for this exact class -- the discriminating gate is not in the gate set CI runs.

issues.issue: PARTIAL MITIGATION with a blind spot. The new static guard correctly (a) asserts opt_stages_precompute.cuh #includes the canonical supergrok11.h and (b) fails any re-inlined `den_m += x*x` / `den_g += x*x` loop -- this would catch a re-inline-style regression. BUT it only scans opt_stages_precompute.cuh, NOT the 3 megakernel files where the actual momentum-operand POINTER is chosen (the `st.exp_avg` argument at fused_*_megakernel.cuh). A regression passing the WRONG base pointer (e.g. st.exp_avg_sq or st.mu) into the canonical sg11_sweep_a_step would not re-inline anything and would pass this guard. The guard is wired into verify_all.py/compile.py (not pytest), which is an acceptable CI hook only if verify_all runs in CI. Recommend extending the scan to assert the SG11 call sites pass st.exp_avg as the momentum argument.
issues.gate_blind_why: The static guard is the other committed defense, but its scan scope (one consumer header, re-inline pattern only) excludes the call-site operand selection, which is precisely where a faithful-looking but wrong-pointer regression would land. Combined with the warm-up not being pytest-collected, both committed regression guards have a hole aligned with the same failure mode.

The code-level analysis shows no mechanism by which the 5 fixes could alter kernel output, so a green gate is expected; this is a verifiability note, not evidence of a red gate.

reports.notes: Re-verified the 5 audit-fixes in eff3e78 at HEAD (3bf77a8) against the actual committed code. VERDICT: SOUND — no gate-blind or correctness issue. The prime suspect (fix 2, .workspace/.n_ctas removal) is provably zero-impact dead-code removal: all 6 launch sites (3 fused_step + 3 sg2_fused_step) read only the 3 barrier counters; the 3 real TC launcher entries declare the workspace param `/*workspace_unused*/` and own their scratch internally; the 3 SG2 entries have no workspace param at all. The fp64 gate (kernel output) IS meaningful here precisely because the workspace was host-side write-only scratch that never reached any kernel — so the dispatch-API/workspace-sizing behavior the gate does NOT cover is also provably unchanged (removed locals total/n_sms/opts_f sized only the deleted tensor; sizing constants and __constant__ size/offset tables are untouched and still used at launch validation). Fixes 1/3 are introspection-only / opt-in-error-path-only (never touch the megakernel production path). Fix 4 is a GENUINE independent structural mirror (does NOT import the oracle's forward/backward — rules out the SG11 co-wrong-oracle failure mode) and adds gate-blind coverage. Fix 5 scan-adapter deletion is zero-#include across all source + build manifests. Files of record: /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp (lines 454-575 structs, 729-1122 fused launch sites, 1240-1359 sg2 launch sites, 272-294 decls), /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_{decoder,vit,mamba}_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu, /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py:545, /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/grokking_optimizers/optimizers/*.py, /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/tests/hw/decoder_kernel_mirror.py. Only caveats are doc-nuances (DOC-1, low sev): the '~9.5MB .so shrink' framing conflates VRAM reclaim (~750MB runtime) with binary size; a stale header name in the mirror docstring; and the GPU fp64 gate re-run is asserted in SESSION_STATE but not re-executable from this read-only CPU sandbox (no mechanism in the 5 fixes could red it — the .so WAS rebuilt post-edit at 05:06 with a clean build.log).
